title: Chapter 3 Quiz 8
description: Making the program decide: If...Then and If...Then...Else.
instructions: Chapter 3: Choice structures: If, Then, Else.
Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What does an **If ... Then ... EndIf** structure do?
options: Runs its actions only if the condition is true
Runs its actions only if the condition is false
Repeats its actions while the condition is true
Runs its actions once, then tests the condition
questions.explanation: The condition is tested, and the actions run only if it is true. Watch out: it is not a loop, and false does not trigger the actions.

questions.question: What is the role of **Else**?
options: Ends the program when the condition is false
Gives the actions to run before the test is done
Gives the actions to run when the condition is false
Repeats the first block when the condition is true
questions.explanation: If...Then...Else chooses between two groups of actions. Watch out: Else never runs when the condition is true.

questions.question: Complete the algorithm that displays the square root of x when x is positive.
questions.code:
Declare x As Integer
Input(x)
{{1}} x > 0 {{2}}
    Let r ← sqrt(x)
    Display(r)
EndIf
questions.explanation: A condition is introduced by If and followed by Then.

questions.question: Complete the algorithm that says whether a number is even or odd.
questions.code:
Read(number)
If number {{1}} 2 = 0 Then
    Display("The number is even.")
{{2}}
    Display("The number is odd.")
EndIf
questions.explanation: An even number has remainder 0 when divided by 2, so we use MOD. The other branch starts with Else. Watch out: DIV gives the quotient, not the remainder.

questions.question: Run the even/odd algorithm for each number and say what is displayed.
questions.explanation: number MOD 2 = 0 means even. Watch out: 0 is even, and -3 is odd.

questions.question: a = 7 and b = 7. The algorithm is: If a > b Then max ← a Else max ← b. What is max?
questions.explanation: 7 > 7 is false, so the Else branch runs and max ← b = 7. Watch out: with equal values the test is false, but the result is still correct.

questions.question: Place the shapes on this flowchart that checks whether x is negative.
questions.explanation: The question is a diamond, the display is a parallelogram and the calculation is a rectangle.

questions.question: In If...Then...Else, the actions of both branches are always executed.
questions.explanation: Only one branch runs, depending on the condition.

questions.question: This should say whether a number is even or odd. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Read(number)
If number DIV 2 = 0 Then
    Display("Even")
Else
    Display("Odd")
EndIf
questions.explanation: Evenness is about the remainder, so we need MOD. Watch out: other tests look similar, but MOD 2 <> 0 would swap the two messages.

questions.question: This should keep the larger of a and b in max. One line is wrong. Find it and type the fix.
questions.code:
Read(a, b)
If a > b Then
    max ← a
Else
    max ← a
EndIf
Display(max)
questions.explanation: If a is not larger than b, the larger value is b. Watch out: the Else branch repeats max ← a, so max is always a.

questions.question: This should display the square root of x only when x is 0 or more. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Read(x)
If x < 0 Then
    Let r ← sqrt(x)
    Display(r)
EndIf
questions.explanation: A square root needs x of 0 or more. Watch out: > 0 would skip zero, and <= 0 would accept negative numbers.
